description:
From examples/keccak.exs (defk-52v.1): writing the round row by row instead of "all 25 rotates, then all of chi" took 16 MB from 40 ms to 27 ms, and rebinding a temporary (`e = bxor(a6, d1)` then rotating `e`) instead of writing it inline put it back to 39 ms, even with `yield: false`. The author could not explain it from the generated C. Likely cause: the 25 lanes plus temporaries exceed the register file, and the compiler's emission (every binding a fresh C local that is also a frame-spill candidate; `(void)` discards; the order of statements) changes clang's register allocation. The kernel runs at 0.55x of ex_keccak (tiny-keccak, plain Rust), so there is a real gap to close.

Investigate with the fast-path report idea (defk-6cn) or by reading the assembly of the two orderings: count spills (stack stores in the hot loop), check whether declaring every local at kernel top (decl_locals) with `= {0}` and the `F->` spill list affects clang's liveness, and whether `yield: false` kernels could declare locals at first use. Record what the two orderings compile to and whether a compiler change (e.g. emitting `const` temporaries, or scoping locals to the block that binds them) recovers the faster ordering regardless of source order.

Done when: the cause is documented in the ticket, and either a compiler change lands with the Keccak example at or near ex_keccak's speed, or the result is recorded as a limit with the recommended source ordering in docs/language.md.

comments.text:
Cause found and fixed (branch defk-zep/keccak-register-pressure, cca7457 + merge of main 3673556).

CAUSE: the DEFK_SP macro spilled EVERY local of the kernel (588 in keccak256) at every safepoint. The Keccak round loop is a short flat loop (24 trips < DEFK_STRIP) with no safepoint inside, but the block loop's safepoint after it stored every round temporary (c, d, b, e, n, a*_next) into F. So clang had to keep each temporary's last-iteration value alive out of the round loop: every temporary became a loop-carried phi, and the round spilled. How many spills depended on statement order and on extra named temporaries, which is why the ordering and `e = bxor(...)` changed the speed. The ticket's "even with yield: false" was yield: false on sponge only: keccak256 inlines sponge with its safepoints, so that had no effect. yield: false on keccak256 itself gave 0 spills in every ordering.

EVIDENCE (cc -S with build.ex's @cflags, stack [sp] stores/loads in the hot round loop, the loop with the most ror; these counts do not depend on machine load). Variants were generated from the example's sponge (scratch generator): rows = row by row (as in the example), all = 25 rotates then all of chi, temp = rotate operand named first.
                 before        after         yield: false (before)
  rows_inline    26 st / 13 ld  9 / 9 (8/8 after merging main)   0 / 0
  all_inline     28 / 18        11 / 11 (6/6)                    0 / 0
  rows_temp      45 / 15        9 / 9 (8/8)                      0 / 0
  all_temp       51 / 21        11 / 11 (6/6)                    0 / 0
Time for 16 MB, best of 7, UNDER LOAD (other agents running): before 27.1 / 29.3 / 37.6 / 41.9 ms; after 20.7 / 21.0 / 21.0 / 21.0 ms; yield: false 18.2-18.6 ms. The order no longer matters.

The kernel-top declarations with `= {0}`, the fresh C local per binding, and the (void) discards do not matter: yield: false kernels have all of them and get 0 spills. clang's mem2reg turns them into SSA. What mattered was liveness from the spill list. So declaring at first use, block scoping, or const temporaries are not needed.

CHANGE (lib/defk/compiler.ex, emission only): fresh/2 records the innermost open loop of each local. in_loop/1 brackets the loop's C with markers (removed before emission). safepoint_saves/2 builds one spill list per safepoint (DEFK_SAVE<n>, pasted into DEFK_SP by token pasting) and leaves out a local bound in the body of loop L when (a) every mention of it in the C is inside L, and (b) L is not a strict ancestor of the safepoint's own loop. Why that is sound: a body binding is written before it is read in every iteration, so it is dead wherever control is not inside an iteration of L, which includes the resume point (the header of the safepoint's loop). Resume restores per safepoint. The frame holds only locals that some safepoint spills. Locals at the top level, and locals of loops that enclose the safepoint, are still spilled as before.

TESTS: new resume shape temps/2 (a body binding read inside and after nested loops, plus an inner-loop temporary), run with natural and forced yields against yield: false, with agreement properties. New test: the spill lists hold `held` at the inner safepoint and never `hot`. Mutation check: dropping body locals at enclosing safepoints too makes the mix shape fail. mix ci passes after merging main (1160 tests). --only deep for resume and agreement: 41 pass.

EXAMPLES (fix vs base, same machine, UNDER LOAD; defk ms):
  keccak 16 MB 27.4 -> 20.7 (ex_keccak 19.1, so 0.92x); batch 10k x 32 B 3.52 -> 3.32 (native 1.97: the gap here is per-message overhead, not the permutation); sha3 16 MB 26.5 -> 21.1
  xxh64 4 MB 0.36-0.40 -> 0.175-0.182 (about 2x); siphash 1k x 32 B 0.054-0.057 -> 0.043-0.044; siphash 4 MB 1.38-1.40 -> 1.44-1.45 in the example (+3%). Standalone, the same kernel's hot loop goes from 45 to 30 instructions with 0 spills (it had 1) and runs 1.40 vs 1.56 ms, so I read the +3% as layout noise in the example.
  fft 1M 36.0 -> 34.1, hash_chain 10M 1761 -> 1678, image_blur 15.8 -> 15.2, rolling_stats 2.34 -> 2.29, murmur3 / crc32c within 1-3% either way, matmul noisy on both sides (1024: 823-837 vs 818-860).
Remaining gap to yield: false (6-11 spills, ~10%) comes from yield bookkeeping live across the loop: follow-up defk-w8l (needs-triage).

title: Keccak-f[1600] permutation: statement order and temporaries change speed by 1.5x (register spills)
